changes.reason: Name s, p and d explicitly so the functions can represent the d-like states that PDWF's s+p PAOs can't. That gives 1+3+5 = 9 functions per Na atom.
Keep all 12 bands the parent has after the 4 semicore bands are excluded, so there's room for 9 functions.
Keep the frozen window at E_F+4 eV, which covers the region the eta_2 weighting scores (up to about E_F+2.5 eV). It holds at most 5 states, below 9 functions.

diagnosis: The construction fails only band_interpolation_eta2 (37 meV, limit 20). This is an interpolation failure, not a subspace-selection failure. On the 11x11x11 mesh every frozen state is reproduced to about 1e-5 eV, but on the path the lowest Wannier band is off by 150-260 meV at E_F+1 to 2.5 eV, inside the frozen window. The real-space Hamiltonian has a long, almost flat hopping tail past 12 Å, and the three p-like functions (spread 6.9 Å², against 3.9 Å² for s) carry it. This is the signature of a 4-function s+p basis forced to contain frozen states it can't describe smoothly: in -4..10 eV the projections are 97% s and only 3% p, so the states above E_F (bands 6-7 from about +1.2 eV, likely d-like near N/H) have little weight on the projectors. Widening the frozen window from E_F+2 to E_F+4 eV moved eta_2 only from 41 to 37 meV, and the window can't widen past 5.68 eV, so the window isn't the instrument. The pseudopotential has no d PAO, so PDWF can't add the missing character. SMV with analytic s, p, d projectors (9 functions, 12 bands available after the semicore cut) can. I couldn't validate the SMV deck because the tool budget for this attempt ran out.

band_interpolation_eta2.note: eta_2 = 2.46 meV at mu = E_F(scf) + 2 = 3.555 eV over 270 path k-points and 9 bands
band_interpolation_eta2.insulator_rule: no band crosses E_F on the mesh and gap >= sigma = 0.1 eV
